tickets.summary: K-3401 NDE bearing vibration rose from 2.1 to 4.6 mm/s in six weeks and remains upward, risking a single-train trip that cuts production within an hour.
tickets.recommended_action: Rotating equipment specialist to diagnose NDE vibration, correct findings, and verify stable running vibration. Obtain source-required attention today. Repeat running vibration and trend review. Specialist diagnose vibration source.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: A strong, unplateaued six-week vibration increase is an advanced progression indicator, although no trip or current function loss is established.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of this non-redundant main export compressor would send the platform to recycle and cut production within an hour.

tickets.summary: FW-8102 failed its first test start, then started after 8 s and reached rated pressure; 22.8 V at rest suggests starting-system degradation, while partner delivery capability is uncertain.
tickets.recommended_action: Inspect batteries and starting air; correct findings, then retest automatic start and rated firewater delivery. Check impairment deviation record. Confirm reliable start and delivery. Load-test batteries and starting air. Test FW-8101 flow and pressure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Required start-on-demand function failed on the first test attempt. Recurrent battery and starting-air problems and the low-side 22.8 V at-rest reading support continuing near-term failure risk despite the successful retry.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure removes one safety-critical firewater pump. FW-8101 is the named redundant partner, but its later test showed only 9.2 barg against 11 barg with flow unmeasured, so capable redundancy cannot yet be credited.

tickets.summary: P-3305 has tripped three times this month and delivered intermittent inhibitor for about ten days; continued starvation can initiate downstream carbon-steel corrosion within weeks.
tickets.recommended_action: Inspect diaphragm and discharge system; repair per findings, then prove sustained pressure and inhibitor injection. Assess downstream corrosion exposure. Check impairment/deviation record. Confirm current pump and repair status. Diagnose diaphragm and discharge path.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The required function is sustained corrosion-inhibitor injection. Three trips in one month and intermittent delivery for around ten days directly demonstrate recurrent function loss.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of the sole inhibitor pump does not stop production, but inhibitor starvation initiates downstream carbon-steel corrosion within weeks, creating a severe delayed integrity consequence.

tickets.recommended_action: Safety authority to assess disposition; inspect dampers and door seals, repair as found, then retest to ≥50 Pa. Check recorded deviation status. Inspect dampers and door seals. Retest TR pressure to ≥50 Pa.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The required pressurisation function failed its test at 27 Pa against a 50 Pa minimum; the fan running at rated speed does not restore the failed envelope-pressure function.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of positive pressure can expose people mustering in the temporary refuge to hydrocarbons during a gas release, and no redundant unit is identified.

tickets.summary: Loose, wind-flapping cladding on the second-stage discharge line threatens to become a dropped object; no process concern is reported, but personnel exposure below is unknown.
tickets.recommended_action: Inspect and control the drop zone; repair or replace cladding fasteners and verify the cladding is secure. Check current cladding security. Check drop-zone personnel exposure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Loose cladding is actively moving in wind and is expected to become a dropped object if left, supporting strong progression toward loss of attachment.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Detachment would create a dropped-object hazard. No process concern is reported, but potential personnel exposure beneath the line is not established.
